candidates.title: Adapting FlexLLMGen to Qwen3 Dense and Mixture-of-Experts Models
candidates.venue: 2026 10th International Conference on Electronic Information Technology and Computer Engineering (EITCE)
candidates.abstract: FlexLLMGen is a representative heterogeneous-memory inference framework, but its original implementation is centered on OPT-style dense decoders and cannot directly run recent Qwen3 dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) checkpoints. This paper presents a two-stage adaptation of FlexLLMGen to Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-30B-A3B. Beyond compatibility itself, the main technical contribution is a scheduler-preserving migration abstraction that separates model-family adaptation into three reusable adapters: configuration translation, checkpoint normalization, and operator replacement, with differential verification as a built-in validation layer. Starting from the original OPT-oriented assumptions in FlexLLMGen, we introduce a Qwen3-specific configuration path, a unified checkpoint-normalization pipeline from Hugging Face safetensors to runtime-consumable numpy weights, and runtime support for RoPE, grouped-query attention, SwiGLU, Q/K normalization, router execution, and shared experts. Experiments cover memory, latency, throughput, sequence-length sensitivity, and a dense output-fidelity proxy under single-GPU heterogeneous offloading. For Qwen3-0.6B, changing from no offloading to CPU/disk-heavy offloading reduces peak GPU memory from 2.039 GB to 1.206 GB, a 40.9% reduction, while end-to-end throughput drops from 9.50 to 5.85 tokens/s at the 64/64 setting. For Qwen3-30B-A3B, the analytical direct-loading baseline is about 60 GB in bf16/fp16 parameter storage, whereas the adapted Flex offloading path completes execution with only 1.716–2.334 GB peak GPU memory, corresponding to about 96.1%–97.1% memory reduction across tested prompt/generation lengths. These results show that the proposed approach makes FlexLLMGen compatible with both Qwen3 dense and Qwen3 MoE models, preserves its offloading-based memory advantage, and offers a reusable migration recipe for other modern dense and sparse decoder families.
candidates.reason: 異種メモリ推論フレームワークFlexLLMGenをQwen3の密・MoE両モデルへ適応させるにあたり、設定変換・チェックポイント正規化・運算子置換の三つの再利用可能アダプタと差分検証でスケジューラ保存型の移行を実現した研究で、オフロード推論基盤の拡張実装として直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: Enhancing Large Language Model Inference Efficiency via Lookahead Cache Filtering
candidates.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
candidates.abstract: The large Key-Value (KV) cache is a significant challenge in deploying Large Language Models (LLMs). Current research addressing these issues employs cache compression techniques, which we find suffer from information loss and the "lost-in-the-middle" problem. We propose the Lookahead Cache Filtering (LCF), which retains the full cache in host memory to keep complete details, using the Important Key-Value Lookahead Prediction by Approximate Sorting and the Gather-based Matrix Multiplication on CPU, to filter important KV cache to reduce the overhead of loading cache to GPU and improve the throughput of inference. Finally, we use the Multi-Scale Pyramid Information Fusion mechanism to enhance information fusion to further improve the effectiveness of inference results. Experiments demonstrate that LCF effectively maintains accuracy without introducing additional latency while reducing memory requirements. Our code will be available on GitHub1.
candidates.reason: KVキャッシュ圧縮の情報損失に対し、全キャッシュをホストメモリに保持したまま先読み予測と近似ソートで重要KVだけをGPUへ集めるLookahead Cache Filteringを提案し、精度を保ちながらメモリ要求を下げる。KVキャッシュ階層利用の機構への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: WAN Cache: Wide-Area Multi-Tier KV Cache Based Inference Acceleration Networks
candidates.abstract: The widespread deployment of Large Language Model (LLM) applications has triggered a massive increase in concurrent inference requests, which poses significant challenges to inference network architectures and systems. As LLM inference expands from single data center to wide-area distributed infrastructure, three key challenges need to be addressed: insufficient KV Cache storage capacity, lack of effective cross-regional cache reuse, and inefficient wide-area transmission. This paper proposes WAN Cache, wide-area multi-tier KV Cache based inference acceleration networks built on a local-edge-cloud hierarchical architecture. Within this framework, this paper presents three core mechanisms: cache-affinity inference request distribution, wide-area multi-tier cache scheduling, and wide-area high-throughput transmission. Through the coordination of these mechanisms, WAN Cache establishes a KV Cache-centric network that optimizes request latency and cache hit rates to scale inference networks across geographically distributed environments. Transmission experiments show that WAN Cache maintains over 75 Gbps throughput under 160 ms Round-Trip Time and 0.1% packet loss in laboratory tests, and achieves approximately 90% bandwidth utilization on a 1,000 km production link in field tests. Caching simulations on real-world LLM workloads show that three-tier cache reduces Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) by up to 48.8% and improves hit rate by up to 42.9 percentage points (pp) over single-tier cache, while cross-cluster sharing reduces TTFT by up to 47.6% and improves hit rate by 32.0 pp over private cache. These results demonstrate that WAN Cache achieves near-local inference performance across wide-area deployments.
candidates.reason: 単一データセンターを超えた広域展開向けに、ローカル・エッジ・クラウドの階層に多層KVキャッシュを置き、キャッシュ親和性に基づくリクエスト分配、多層キャッシュスケジューリング、広域高スループット伝送を備えたWAN Cacheを提案する。KVキャッシュ中心の推論基盤への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: Crowd: An KV Cache Eviction Policy Which Uses Crowd Information to Select Evicted Key-Value Pairs
candidates.venue: 2024 4th International Conference on Computer Science and Blockchain (CCSB)
candidates.abstract: Although large language models have been widely applied in various aspects of daily life, it is worth noting that, in addition to their substantial demand for computational resources, they also require an exceptionally large amount of GPU memory. This is because, aside from the model weights, the key-value cache must also be stored in GPU memory, and the size of this cache increases with the batch size and sequence length, becoming a significant bottleneck in inference. In this paper, we introduce an innovative method for optimizing key-value (KV) cache, significantly reducing its memory usage. Through experimental validation, we observed that the higher the similarity between query vectors, the higher the similarity between the key vectors they attend to. Additionally, experiments showed that the vectors most similar to the current query vector are concentrated within its local window size. Based on these findings, we propose a new KV cache eviction policy called Crowd, which can dynamically select the necessary key-value pairs for inference without requiring model retraining or fine-tuning. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of Crowd during both the pre-filling and autoregressive decoding stages.
candidates.reason: クエリベクトル同士の類似性が高いほど注視するキーの類似性も高く、かつ局所ウィンドウ内に集中するという観測に基づき、再学習なしで必要なKVペアを動的に残すKVキャッシュ削除ポリシーCrowdを提案する。KVメモリ削減機構への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: Accelerated Dynamic Quantization and Semantic Pruning for Large Language Models on Edge Communication Devices
candidates.venue: 2025 4th International Joint Conference on Information and Communication Engineering (JCICE)
candidates.abstract: Large language models have demonstrated strong performance in natural language processing tasks, but their high computational and memory demands hinder deployment on edge devices. To address this, we propose a lightweight inference acceleration method combining three techniques: dynamic activation quantization, semantic-aware pruning, and input-adaptive pruning scheduling. The method dynamically adjusts quantization parameters based on per-layer activation distributions to mitigate accuracy loss from outliers. It further incorporates word embeddings and syntactic features to assess token importance, enabling fine-grained, semantics-driven token pruning. Pruning strength is adaptively adjusted based on input length, improving adaptability across scenarios. Experiments show that our method achieves up to $2.8 \times$ inference speedup without compromising model performance, outperforming standalone weight quantization or attention pruning.
candidates.reason: エッジ通信デバイス向けに、層ごとの活性分布で量子化パラメータを動的に調整する動的活性量子化と、意味を考慮したトークンプルーニング、入力長適応のプルーニングスケジューリングを組み合わせ、最大2.8倍の推論高速化を示す。エッジLLM推論高速化への直接貢献である。
